summary: Hightower Labs bulk data-migration triggered massive fan-out -> Dedicated GPU pool exhaustion, automated fallback to hosted, duplicate completions and billing exposure
description:
Issue summary:
On 2026-03-12 during a scheduled bulk data migration by Hightower Labs, an unexpected client-side retry behavior caused a high fan-out of inference requests to their Dedicated pool. Autoscaler and scheduler logic treated the surge as consistent traffic, which led to GPU pool exhaustion and an automated fallback to the hosted API tier. The hosted fallback accepted the inflight load while the Dedicated control plane attempted scale-up, resulting in duplicate completions for many requests and a material billing exposure for the customer.

Impact:
- Customer-facing latencies spiked to 6-12s for streaming responses during the event window (approx 10:07-10:42 UTC).
- ~18% of Hightower's requests received duplicate completions (confirmed via request_id parity and transcript diffs).
- Billing exposure estimated ~$4.2k for the incident window.
- Customer reported degraded user experience and opened an escalation to account exec.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool id: dp-htw-us-east-04
- Region: us-east
- Models: gptx-3.8 (primary), gptx-3.8-quantized (fallback)

Steps to reproduce (from customer reproduction run):
1) Kick off Hightower ETL job that issues ~20k parallel inference requests over 10 minutes with a 1s client retry on 5xx.
2) Observe scheduler crediting requests to the pool and autoscaler marking nodes for scale-up.
3) Simulate transient throttling from manifest service to force some inflight requests to be retried by client.
4) Confirm duplicate completions when fallback routing happens mid-request.

Logs / telemetry pointers:
- Incident timeline: link to incident runbook in Slack (#inc-hightower) and INC-2026-03-12-07
- Grafana: /d/redwood/serving-runtime?orgId=1&var-pool=dp-htw-us-east-04 (CPU/GPU utilization spike at 10:08)

investigation_notes:
10:05-10:20 UTC: ETL window begins. Serving runtime sees sudden 8x increase in short-lived streams.
Hypothesis: Client retry loop combined with parallel migration tasks caused amplification.

10:22 UTC: Scheduler backlog grows. Autoscaler computes scale target but cloud provisioning lag prevents timely node joins.
Partial finding: node bootpack time averages 6-8 minutes in this region under burst conditions.

10:32 UTC: Fallback to hosted tier triggered by capacity circuit. Some requests were already partially processed on Dedicated; fallback completed duplicates.
Finding: fallback logic does not mark already-inflight requests for idempotency at the routing layer.

10:40 UTC: Streaming backpressure observed; some clients closed streams and retried, creating additional load.
Finding: client retry policy (1s retry on 5xx, exponential backoff disabled) was primary amplification vector.

Confirmed root causes: 1) Customer-side aggressive retry during a large-scale migration, 2) Dedicated pool provisioning latency (cloud node boot delay), 3) Routing/fallback semantics that allow duplicate completions when fallback triggers mid-request.
Telemetry artifacts: request_id duplication reports, KV cache mismatch traces, and token accounting spikes. See Grafana panels and logs at /d/redwood/serving-runtime (dp-htw-us-east-04).
resolution_notes:
Immediate mitigations executed on 2026-03-12:
- Throttled Hightower account traffic at edge (rate-limit override) to stop amplification.
- Paused their ETL bulk job upon customer request.
- Drained fallback traffic and initiated cleanup of duplicate completions from the transcript store.

Short-term fixes deployed 2026-03-13:
- Rollout of routing patch to mark inflight requests 'in-progress' and block duplicate completion in fallback (hotfix PR #4567).
- Autoscaler tuning: lower threshold to trigger scale earlier for Dedicated pools during sustained short-lived streams.
- Issued customer credit of $4,250 as preliminary goodwill; Finance to finalize.

Action items for follow-up (owners and due dates):
- SRE (Arjun) to add autoscaler provisioning benchmark and alert if node boot > 4m under burst (due 2026-03-21).
- Serving Runtime (R&D lead: Mei Chen) to design idempotency markers for inflight routing to prevent duplicate completions (MVP by 2026-04-09).
- Developer Docs (DX) to publish best-practice for bulk workloads including recommended client retry/backoff (due 2026-03-19).
- Account team to coordinate a controlled migration window with rate caps for Hightower and enable a dedicated pre-warm flow (Account PM: Lucas Grant).
Postmortem scheduled: 2026-03-15 14:00 UTC. Postmortem page created and invited participants: SRE, Runtime, Product, Billing, Hightower engineers.
